item.title: Tajikistan Independence Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Tajikistan Independence Day

Press Statement

September 8, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend warm congratulations to the people of Tajikistan as they celebrate 35 years of independence on September 9.

The United States and Tajikistan share a strong interest in a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Central Asia. Our cooperation on border security and counterterrorism helps protect both of our countries and contributes to regional stability. Tajikistan’s hosting of the B5+1 Forum in Dushanbe will provide an important opportunity to strengthen regional economic cooperation and expand trade and investment, including opportunities for American businesses.

As Tajikistan celebrates this important anniversary, the United States remains committed to strengthening our partnership and working together to advance security and economic opportunities. We look forward to deepening the ties between our peoples and supporting greater prosperity for both of our countries.

item.title: Secretary Rubio and Colombian Foreign Minister Bula Sign Arrangements on Critical Minerals and Civil Nuclear Cooperation
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Secretary Rubio and Colombian Foreign Minister Bula Sign Arrangements on Critical Minerals and Civil Nuclear Cooperation

Fact Sheet

September 8, 2026

During Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s trip to Barranquilla, Colombia, on September 8, he and Colombian Foreign Minister Omar Bula signed two arrangements to advance cooperation in the fields of critical minerals and civil nuclear cooperation.  These arrangements are part of our countries’ efforts to reinvigorate the over 200-year U.S.-Colombia partnership and restore it as a linchpin of security and economic cooperation in our hemisphere.

The Critical Minerals Framework:

  • Establishes a U.S.-Colombia framework to secure resilient, diversified, and fair supply chains for critical minerals and rare earths, committing both governments to mobilize government and private sector support—via guarantees, loans, equity, offtake arrangements, insurance, or regulatory facilitation—to jointly identify and finance mining and processing projects within six months of signing.
  • Calls for streamlined permitting, market-protective pricing mechanisms such as price floors, national security review tools for critical minerals asset sales, investment in minerals recycling technology, and cooperation on geological mapping.

The Civil Nuclear Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding:

  • Establishes a bilateral framework for strategic civil nuclear cooperation between the United States and Colombia, grounded in Non-Proliferation Treaty obligations and International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, as Colombia considers deploying nuclear power to advance energy security and deepen the two countries’ broader strategic relationship.
  • Expresses joint intent to collaborate across regulatory capacity-building, industry partnerships, and scientific and academic exchanges to support Colombia’s civil nuclear infrastructure and workforce development; explore U.S. nuclear technologies (including advanced and small modular reactors), fuel, equipment, and services; and pursue both power and non-power applications such as research reactors, radioisotopes, nuclear medicine, agriculture, and waste management—all while upholding the highest standards of safety, security, and non-proliferation.

For media inquiries, please contact the Office of the Spokesman.

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to Press
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Homestead, Florida

Homestead Air Reserve Base

Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to Press

Remarks

September 8, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  So this is an important trip, obviously.  We’re going to go visit three countries strongly aligned with the United States.  We have a lot of common interests with them, both taking on regional transnational criminal terrorism and also economic engagements.  We’re hoping to wrap up good, solid trade deals with all three of these countries in the foreseeable future.  And of course, a lot of strong cultural links.

So I think it’s part of a trend that you’re seeing in the Western Hemisphere of alignment with the U.S. and U.S. interests.  If you read our National Security Strategy – I’m sure all of you have read it very carefully page by page – it outlines one of our priorities is strengthening our presence in the Western Hemisphere.  And I think this trip and these meetings, as much as anything else, is continuing to further that goal as part of that strategy.

QUESTION:  Secretary Rubio, why not travel to Venezuela on this trip?  As you mentioned, this is all about the Western Hemisphere. 

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, we’ll get there eventually, as I said, but you can’t go everywhere.  This is a condensed week, obviously, with Labor Day yesterday and then 9/11 on – on Friday that we’ll be commemorating the 25th anniversary.  So we just simply couldn’t add another, and these are countries we needed to get to that I hadn’t gotten to yet.

So in the case of Colombia, they just had a free and democratic election.  They elected someone I know very well, very aligned with the U.S., and we want to – we have a longstanding relationship.  In the case of Peru, after some political turmoil, they too have had a recent election, and President Fujimori is someone we look forward to engaging with.  And then in Ecuador, obviously, their election was last year but they face – they’re one of our closest security partners in the region, and I think there’s more we can do with them – economics as well.

QUESTION:  Secretary Rubio, what would your message be to Latin Americans who might look at the Venezuela oil deal and think that the U.S. Government’s interested in extracting resources or just sending troops?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, I —

QUESTION:  What’s your message?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, what I would say to anyone who is concerned that the U.S. is doing something negative towards the Western Hemisphere as regards to energy is those oil fields, once dominated by China and Russia and Iran, by the way; Iran also had some concessions – and they’re no longer there.  So I think they’re much better off partnering with the United States.  They will benefit greatly from it.  These fields were in many cases nonproductive; in essence, the Chinese and Russian companies held these fields but never turned them into anything.  These fields are going to be productive and they’re going to generate royalties and revenues for the Venezuelan people – eventually through a democratically elected government, hopefully sooner rather than later – and directly benefit the people of Venezuela, as opposed to going into the pocket of some corrupt government official or in the hands of American and Venezuelan adversaries, really.

QUESTION:  Mr. Secretary, do you have anything to say about the British decision on the imports from Israel – or from settlements in —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, they alerted us to it.  We don’t have any announcements.  Obviously, these are decisions that they make.  And we and the President has expressed this in the past:  We don’t want to see anything destabilizing going on right now in the West Bank with so much going on in the region.  We think it has implications as well on our ability to make progress with regards to Gaza and the 20-point plan and Board of Peace that we’re very committed to.  Obviously, we’re not going to do what the UK did.  We saw their announcement today, but I don’t have any comment on it right now.

QUESTION:  But Ambassador Huckabee said that you’ve – that the Brits will suffer because of that with the U.S., that he suggested that the U.S. —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, I would say that the President has not commented on this.  As I said, neither have I at this point.  We were made aware that they were going to make this decision.  We heard their arguments as to why.  But look, we share the goal of stability.  We don’t want to see some uptick in violence or an uptick in conflict or tensions in the West Bank at a very tenuous time in the region.  There’s always tenuous times.  But beyond that, I don’t think – as of this moment, we don’t have any further comment on the UK decision that I think was announced just a few hours ago. 

QUESTION:  Overnight the Houthis launched a substantial attack on Saudi Arabia.  What are your thoughts on that when the U.S. has put pressure on the Houthis to kind of stay out of this fight?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah, look, again, the Houthis in many ways are agents and proxies of the Iranians.  I think behind some of this is clearly the Iranian hand.  The U.S. has a very strong defensive military relationship with Saudi Arabia, and we’re watching those events very closely.  It’s been going on for some time.  I think there’s been some ground operations as well where many forces are taking on the Houthis and pushing back against some of the ground advances that they attempted to make.  And we’re monitoring that, as I said, very, very closely.  And – but I would defer as far as on the defense side to the Department of War.  I don’t think there’ll be any announcements on that today.

item.title: Operation Economic Outcast Grounds Iran’s Aviation Sector
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson

Operation Economic Outcast Grounds Iran’s Aviation Sector

Press Statement

September 8, 2026

Today, the United States continues implementation of Operation Economic Outcast by sanctioning 36 entities and individuals in multiple jurisdictions for aiding Iran’s aviation sector. This sector has enabled the regime to support proliferation and terrorism worldwide.

On August 24, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) determined that Executive Order (E.O.) 13902 shall apply to Iran’s aviation sector, among others.  Under that authority, OFAC is designating the remainder of Iran’s active airlines, furthering our campaign to isolate the Iranian regime from the international system and global economy.  Today, OFAC is also targeting several third country‑based firms that have provided cargo and general sales services to, and procured aircraft for, Iran’s largest airline, Mahan Air, which has been designated in connection to the regime’s proliferation and terrorism-support activities around the world.

We will not relent in our campaign to shut down the Iranian regime’s financial lifelines, including the aviation sector. 

Today’s actions are being taken pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority, and E.O. 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy. On October 12, 2011, OFAC designated Mahan Air pursuant to E.O. 13224 for providing financial, material, and technological support to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Quds Force (IRGC-QF), which OFAC designated pursuant to E.O. 13224 in October 2007 for providing support to multiple terrorist organizations.  On December 11, 2019, the U.S. Department of State designated Mahan Air pursuant to E.O. 13382, which targets weapons of mass destruction (WMD) proliferators and their supporters. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s Press Release.

item.title: Andorra National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Andorra National Day

Press Statement

September 8, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend warm wishes to the people of Andorra as they celebrate their patron saint, Our Lady of Meritxell.

The United States values Andorra as a steadfast friend that shares our commitment to national sovereignty and a secure, prosperous future for its citizens. The United States is proud of the momentum built over the past year in our relationship with the Principality of Andorra, particularly Andorra’s continued collaboration with American technology companies to strengthen its digital infrastructure and financial sector security. We look forward to building on this foundation in the coming year, expanding opportunities for U.S. businesses and investment.

As the people of Andorra celebrate this important day, the United States reaffirms its partnership with the Principality and extends our warmest regards to the Andorran people in the year ahead.

Eswatini National Day

Press Statement

September 6, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I offer warm congratulations to the citizens of Eswatini as you mark the 58th anniversary of your nation’s independence. The enduring bond between our two countries demonstrates a mutual dedication to stability, community health, and prosperity. We welcome further collaboration and productive exchanges that strengthen our security, resilience, and success.

Please accept our heartfelt best wishes on this joyous occasion.

item.title: U.S. Sanctions Dismantle the Iranian Regime’s Revenue Streams
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson

U.S. Sanctions Dismantle the Iranian Regime’s Revenue Streams

Press Statement

September 4, 2026

The United States remains committed to cutting off the Iranian regime’s access to the international financial system and the resources it uses to destabilize the region and threaten U.S. interests and partners. Today’s U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctions on Türkiye-based Golden Global Bank mark the latest step in Operation Economic Outcast, a whole-of-government effort to sever the networks that allow the regime to launder funds, evade sanctions, and finance its terrorist proxies across the Middle East.

This action sends a clear message to financial institutions worldwide: facilitating Iran’s illicit financial activity carries serious consequences. This demonstrates the Trump Administration’s commitment to eliminating resources the regime uses to threaten regional stability, support terrorism, and advance its military capabilities.

The United States will continue to use every diplomatic and economic tool at its disposal to isolate the Iranian regime until it abandons its support for terrorism and its destabilizing activities in the region. We urge the international community to join this effort and ensure no institution serves as a financial lifeline for a regime that threatens peace and security.

Today’s action is being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the financial sector of Iran’s economy and advances Operation Economic Outcast—a campaign to completely isolate the regime from the financial lifelines that sustain its malign behavior. Please see the Department of the Treasury’s Press Release.

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Travel to Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson

Secretary Rubio’s Travel to Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru

Press Statement

September 4, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru from September 8-10 to strengthen key U.S. partnerships in our region. During the trip, he will meet with the new De La Espriella government in Colombia, President Noboa in Ecuador, and the new Fujimori government in Peru to discuss U.S. support for Colombia’s earthquake response; enhanced cooperation in the shared fight against narcoterrorism, which threatens our hemisphere; and the benefits of deeper commercial relationships between our countries.

Throughout the trip, the Secretary will reaffirm the Trump Administration’s commitment to a secure, prosperous, and democratic Western Hemisphere.

item.title: Quad Sherpas’ Meeting in New Delhi
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Quad Sherpas’ Meeting in New Delhi

Media Note

September 3, 2026

India’s Foreign Secretary Shri Vikram Misri hosted a Quad Sherpas’ Meeting in New Delhi on September 3, 2026. The meeting was attended by Ms. Elly Lawson, Deputy Secretary, Strategic Planning & Coordination Group, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Australia; Mr. Hiroyuki Namazu, Senior Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs, Japan; and Mr. Sergio Gor, Special Envoy to South and Central Asia and Ambassador of USA to India.

The Quad Sherpas’ Meeting follows the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in New Delhi on May 26, 2026 and was convened to take forward its outcomes and to prepare for the next Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

The Sherpas reviewed progress across ongoing Quad initiatives and discussed ways to further strengthen practical cooperation, with a shared commitment to advancing a free and open Indo-Pacific.

Discussions covered key areas of Quad cooperation, including maritime and transnational security; economic prosperity and security; critical and emerging technologies; and humanitarian assistance and emergency response. The Sherpas also exchanged views on developments in the Indo-Pacific and the broader regional and global context.

The Quad Sherpas reaffirmed the importance of focusing on concrete, action-oriented initiatives. They looked forward to continued consultations in the lead-up to the next Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

item.title: Further Sanctions on Cuba’s Elites, Financial Channels, and Resource Exploitation Apparatus
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Further Sanctions on Cuba’s Elites, Financial Channels, and Resource Exploitation Apparatus

Press Statement

September 3, 2026

The Communist Cuban regime continues to pose a deep, multifaceted threat to U.S. national security and our hemisphere’s stability. While the Cuban people suffer, the Castro family and their cronies in Cuba’s repressive Ministry of the Interior (MININT) continue to perpetuate their total control of the island’s economy, hoarding resources for the benefit of a small group of regime elites. Today, pursuant to President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, “Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and for Threats to United States National Security and Foreign Policy,” I am designating five entities and one individual whose activities prop up the regime’s financial services, metals and mining, and energy sectors, and are part of networks that advance the regime’s threats to U.S. national security.

Among those designated today are a grandson of Raúl Castro, Fidel Ernesto Castro Calis, Banco Exterior de Cuba, and four entities exploiting Cuba’s natural resources or energy reserves for the benefit of the regime.
